title: Gesture-friendly modal compression and CSS-reset interop for console surfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Improve modal and overlay behaviour across viewport sizes and legacy/quirky browser CSS resets. Focus on touch gestures, compressed modal states for narrow screens, and robust interop with customer and third-party CSS (reset styles, UA tweaks). Deliver a prototype and implementation guidance for engineering that avoids layout thrash and preserves keyboard/navigation semantics.
background: Several customer support threads and telemetry indicate modals and embedded charts misbehave on narrow viewports and older browser builds. Problems include: fullscreen modals being scroll-locked but not visually clipped on iOS Safari; chart overlays causing heavy reflow when toggling dense mode; third-party widgets injecting global resets that break our backdrop layering and focus trapping. Design must produce defensible defaults and fallback strategies while staying consistent with Redwood Console visual language.
goals: Define compressed modal states for <=480px width that prioritize primary actions and preserve contextual breadcrumbs
Document and prototype CSS patterns that are resilient when an upstream CSS reset or normalization is present
Provide gesture-first interaction patterns (swipe-to-dismiss, drag-to-resize) that degrade gracefully on non-touch platforms
Minimize layout reflow on modal open/close and when toggling dense/compact table/chart modes
Produce an implementation checklist and QA matrix for engineering across Chrome, Safari (iOS + macOS), and Firefox
acceptance_criteria: Compressed modal variant implemented in prototype with a11y focus trap and visible focus ring
Prototype demonstrates swipe-to-dismiss on iOS simulators and keyboard fallback (Esc) on desktop
CSS guidance document includes selectors/namespaces to avoid breakage from third-party resets
Performance measurement shows modal open/close does not cause >3 forced reflows for typical dashboard payload (charts + tables)
Cross-browser QA matrix completed with pass/fail notes for Chrome 120+, Safari 17+, iOS Safari, and Firefox 118+
tasks: Design compressed modal wireframes (A/B) and mark interaction hotspots
Build clickable Figma prototype with touch gestures mapped to progressive states
Run lightweight instrumented bench on an example dashboard to measure reflow counts
Draft CSS interop pattern doc: namespace requirements, reset-safe variables, and utility classes
Pair with frontend eng to implement a conservative JS open/close path avoiding layout thrash
Create QA checklist and run cross-browser tests (visual + interaction)
progress_updates: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: scoped problem with eng and PM. Agreed to prioritize iOS Safari scroll locking and CSS-reset interop.
2025-02-20 - Initial wireframes reviewed by PM (Jonah Mercer) and accessibility lead (Priya Raman). Action: add visible focus affordance for dense state.
2025-02-26 - Prototype built: swipe-to-dismiss gesture flows added. Early feedback: swipe velocity threshold too aggressive on older iPadOS builds.

2025-03-01 - Pair session with frontend (Marco Liu) to review implementation options. Decided to prefer transform-based animations (translateY + opacity) to avoid reflow; add a compact-content clipping layer to isolate canvas paints.

2025-03-05 - Perf bench landed on internal branch; modal open path reduced forced reflows from 12 to 2 on sample dashboard when using transform-based approach. Further testing scheduled across Firefox.
review_feedback: PM Jonah Mercer: prefer consistent affordance for primary action across compressed and full modals; do not hide primary action behind expandable content
Accessibility Priya Raman: ensure focus trap is preserved in compressed states and provide clear skip link for keyboard users
Frontend Marco Liu: implement a small JS microtask to defer non-essential DOM writes to reduce layout thrash during open animation
Design Lead Elena Garcia: add visual token for 'compressed header' to reuse across Rollouts and Cost Explorer modals
decisions: Use transform-based show/hide animations for modals (translateY + opacity) to leverage compositor when possible
Introduce a namespaced CSS reset guard (.rw-reset-safe) that scoped third-party resets should opt into; document how to wrap embedded widgets
Compressed modal retains breadcrumb + primary CTA visible; secondary actions collapse into an overflow menu
Expose a 'dense' CSS utility class for engineering to flip spacing/typography inside modal content without re-mounting heavy chart canvases
tradeoffs: Transform approach reduces reflows but requires added JS bookkeeping to handle height measurement for accessible announcements
Compressed modal reduces content surface on small viewports which can hide tertiary context; mitigated by breadcrumb and explicit 'show more' affordance
Namespaced reset guard requires coordination with 3rd-party widget teams; initial rollouts may need embedding wrappers which increase integration effort
risks: Old browser builds (Safari <15, Firefox ESR) may fallback to repaint-heavy path leading to jank on low-end devices
Third-party analytics widgets that inject global styles could still interfere if integrators do not apply the namespace
Gesture thresholds tuned on simulators may not match real-world device variability; will need field validation
next_steps: Finalize Figma prototype and handoff token table to frontend (target 2025-03-07)
Frontend to implement prototype branch with transform-based animations and dense utility (target PR by 2025-03-14)
QA to run cross-browser matrix including iPadOS 15-17, desktop Safari, Chrome, and Firefox (target 2025-03-18)
Follow-up: run limited rollout to 10% of traffic on dedicated infra and collect interaction metrics and error reports
